headline: 27 contracts catalogued across Solana, Ethereum, and Stellar (4 Solana program/mint addresses, 12 Ethereum pool contracts across 2 pools, 10 Stellar contracts, 1 BSC token); Monad addresses not yet live; HUMA governance token EVM addresses surfaced only as snippets pending on-chain verification.

findings.text: D1: Block-explorer name-tag search: BscScan snippet surfaced HUMA token at 0x92516e0ddf1ddbf7fab1b79cac26689fdc5ba8e6 (BEP-20); ethplorer snippet surfaced HUMA token on Ethereum at 0x86F31c73975D2de4788EeF972f128Fde8F4bea13. Both are snippet-only — no full block-explorer page fetched; recorded in unknowns per D8. Etherscan direct fetch was allowlist-blocked (URL not pre-fetched). Solana, Stellar, and Monad explorers not directly fetchable this run.

D2: Official deployed contracts doc found at https://docs.huma.finance/ecosystem-resources/smart-contracts — full page fetched. Lists Solana program addresses (Huma, Huma Institutional), Solana account mints (PST, mPST), EVM addresses for Arf 3-month and Arf 6-month pools (PoolConfig, JuniorTranche, PoolSafe, SeniorTranche, CreditManager, Credit each), and 10 Stellar contract addresses. deployed_contracts_doc set to this URL.

D3: Audit page fetched at https://docs.huma.finance/ecosystem-resources/security-audits. Auditors: Halborn (Solana programs, 2 reports + incremental), Sec3 (Solana programs, 4 reports including incremental), Spearbit (EVM, 2 reports — commit SHA 21aaad53 confirmed from GitHub fetch), Certora (Stellar). Bug bounty via Spearbit/Cantina confirmed. Audit PDFs are linked but PDF content extraction not available this run; no contract address tables extracted from PDFs directly.

D4: GitHub org is 00labs (https://github.com/00labs). Repos identified: huma-contracts (v1 EVM, hardhat-deploy with goerli-deployed-contracts.json pattern), huma-contracts-v2 (EVM v2, contains audit/ folder; develop branch commit 21aaad53023eb3f448ff09820fee1a3936b6175d confirmed). Deployment artifact files (broadcast/run-latest.json or deployments/*.json) not directly fetched this run due to tool-call limits — recorded in unknowns.

D5: Multi-chain enumeration: Ethereum — 12 EVM pool contract addresses catalogued from docs page. Solana — 4 addresses (2 programs, 2 mints) from docs page. Stellar — 10 addresses from docs page (JuniorTranche and SeniorTranche share same address CDJ6AO57... — possible docs error noted). Monad — listed in protocol.chains but no contracts surfaced from any source; likely pre-launch. BSC — HUMA token snippet from BscScan; snippet-only, in unknowns.

D6: ContractFactory at Stellar address CBQHYENQ7ANK5UEUOGEL5CMLZV3LUPS4IVR3EHXMMVYQTNMFOGPTLXBC identified; Stellar chain not supported by DeFiPunkd read API (only EVM chains listed). Factory enumeration on EVM not yet possible — no factory address surfaced for EVM. Recorded in unknowns.

D7: Role taxonomy applied. All EVM pool contracts classified as 'pool' or 'vault' (PoolSafe). Stellar ContractFactory classified as 'factory', HumaConfig as 'admin' (protocol-wide config). Solana programs classified as 'other' (program/runtime). Admin multisig addresses not yet surfaced from any fetchable source — docs state all admin functions secured with multisigs but do not list multisig addresses.

D8: HUMA Ethereum token (0x86F31c73975D2de4788EeF972f128Fde8F4bea13) and BSC token (0x92516e0ddf1ddbf7fab1b79cac26689fdc5ba8e6) surfaced from search snippets only — not from full fetched page bodies. Excluded from admin_addresses per D8 rule; recorded in unknowns for next run.

protocol_metadata.about: Huma Finance is a PayFi (Payment Finance) network that enables on-chain payment financing across Solana, Ethereum, Stellar, and Monad. Users — including businesses and individuals — can access short-term credit lines backed by real-world receivables (invoices, cross-border settlement flows), while liquidity providers deposit stablecoins into tranched pools to earn yield from real payment activities. The protocol issues PST (principal stablecoin token) on Solana as a tradable receipt for LP deposits, and structures institutional lending through permissioned EVM pools. All administrative functions are stated to be secured by multisigs, with smart contracts engineered to prevent admin access to user funds.
